newsitem.title: USA: Pall sees no Q4 dilution from Gelman deal.
newsitem.headline: Pall sees no Q4 dilution from Gelman deal.

text.p: Pall Corp said Wednesday that it did not expect the consolidation of Gelman Sciences Inc to dilute earnings in its fourth quarter.
Pall, which acquired Gelman last year, said the operation diluted earnings by about $0.02 a share in the third quarter.

The company, which makes filters and other devices for sectors like healthcare, said it expected exchange rates to reduce fourth quarter sales by three percent at current rates even though it saw the rates improving from the previous quarter.

Pall said it foresaw the health care market remaining "sluggish" and the semiconductor industry maintaining its decline in the next quarter. "(This) will result in flat sales on a unit and price basis," it said.
The company said it was nevertheless optimistic about the next fiscal year.
"Gelman will be accretive and our other restructuring will enhance the bottom line," it said.
"We and others forecast general improvement in the semiconductor and health care markets and there are significant new products that will be contributing to sales in each of our markets," it added.
Pall reported a net loss of $0.18 per share for the quarter, compared to last year's profit of $0.32.

"This result is due to the effects of one-time charges (including the Gelman Sciences merger and restructuring charges) of $92,019,000, equal to 47 cents per share (after pro forma tax effect)," it said.
Sales in the third quarter totaled $275.3 million against $277.4 million a year ago, it said.
It said sales were reduced four percent due to foreign currency exchange rates.
